opportunities.name: InsurTech America Innovation Challenge 2026 (The Hartford / Travelers prize categories)
opportunities.agency: InsurTech America (InsurTech Hartford); categories sponsored by The Hartford and Travelers
opportunities.amount: $10,000 cash per category: 'Future of Customer Protection Award' (The Hartford) and 'Best Emerging Product / Service' (Travelers). One startup from the challenge also qualifies for the Startup World Cup (a $1,000,000 INVESTMENT prize, so equity, not a grant). The student category is for CT students only.
opportunities.summary: DEADLINE IN 5 DAYS (7 Oct 2026), AND THE CHALLENGE IS FRAMED AROUND INSURANCE. This is the only corporate or payer challenge in this lane that pays cash and is open today. To fit, pitch Vybe as risk prevention: continuous HRV/ECG-derived recovery and sleep signals that help insurers and employers 'predict, prevent, quantify, and manage risk'. Past rounds had a Hartford category seeking 'remote monitoring, coaching, and care delivery' for insureds' health and safety, which is close to Vybe. Pitch it as wellness and risk insight, never diagnosis. The page does not state a fee, entry documents or a revenue cap. Read the form before submitting. The submission link on the official LinkedIn posts is lnkd.in/gfg5dGDf. Finalists are announced 20 Oct; a mentorship program follows (Nov to Feb). Travel to Hartford is at Vybe's own cost (not stated otherwise).
opportunities.eligibility: Open to 'startups, scale-ups, and innovators from across the insurance ecosystem'. The page states no application fee, no geographic gate and no age gate. The CT Student Seed Fund category is limited to Connecticut students; Vybe should enter one of the two open $10K categories. Finalists present in person in Hartford, CT on 27 Oct 2026.
documents: Online submission form (contents not stated on the public page; expect a company and solution description)
Finalists: a live pitch at the Showcase & Awards on 27 Oct 2026

opportunities.name: Rutgers Health Hack 2026
opportunities.agency: Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School / RWJ University Hospital
opportunities.amount: $10,000 in cash, divided among multiple winning teams (split not stated)

The 2025 edition had a Women's Health track and an App Building track; 2026 tracks are not yet posted (ruhealthhack.com still shows 2025). Best as a low-cost way to recruit clinical design partners plus a shot at cash.

documents: Project requirements 'revealed in person at hackathon'

opportunities.amount: $1,500 in cash total per Devpost (one cash prize per track; the per-track amount is 'to be announced')

The Healthcare track (language, coverage, access for underserved patients) suits a minority-owned team that builds a Connect/Vitals community-health demo. IP: 'You keep everything you build. opportunities.name: eMerge Americas NatSec Veteran Pitch Competition (Nov 2026 cycle)
opportunities.amount: Not cash-denominated on the page: the top three get Demo Day participation at PortMiami (2 Mar 2027), Accelerator and Showcase fast-tracks, exhibition space in the NatSec Pavilion and investor/government-buyer introductions. A prior cycle listed micro-grants among prizes, but no cash figure is stated for this cycle.

Vybe fits only if it frames the Vybe Band (ECG/HRV, recovery, readiness) as a warfighter human-performance and readiness tool. The veteran owner has to pitch. Virtual event on 4 Nov 2026, with no registration fee. The deadline is 9 days away.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S.-based critical-technology startup founded within the last 3 years; working MVP; 2+ full-time team members; no more than $1M raised; a veteran, active or reserve service member must be a founder or C-level exec and must deliver the pitch; technology must be presentable unclassified.
documents: Online application (details on the application page; contents not stated on the announcement page)
Pitch deck for a 4-minute virtual pitch if selected

opportunities.name: AgeTech After Dark @ CES 2027 — AARP pitch
opportunities.amount: $10,000 grand prize; every finalist gets a complimentary CES 2027 ticket
opportunities.summary: Eleven days out and the cheapest $10K on the board to try for: an online application, then a 3-minute pitch in Las Vegas on 7 Jan 2027. Vybe qualifies through the healthspan-and-wellness door — the pitch should be personal health intelligence for people over 50, not a repositioned ageing product. Pitching also makes Vybe eligible for the AARP accelerator already on the board. The page names no application fee. Getting to Las Vegas is Vybe's cost; the CES ticket is not.
opportunities.eligibility: AgeTech startups, and explicitly healthspan and wellness products that help people 'stay in the game' as they age. Prototypes welcome but they want market-ready products
documents: Online application: how the product makes ageing easier, and its stage
A 3-minute pitch, ready by early January

opportunities.name: Veteran Shark Tank 2026 (13th annual)
opportunities.amount: $50,000 to the winner; five veteran entrepreneurs pitch live
opportunities.summary: CLOSES 13 OCT — the best-fitting live item on the board for a company under a year old, because its age test runs the opposite way to everyone else's. Buckeye wants two years and Tadlock wants one; this one wants under three. Entry is a form plus a 2-minute narrated pitch video and a deck of no more than 10 slides covering market, product, go-to-market, customers, financials and key risks. No application fee is named anywhere on the application page. The 2016 winner was NeuroFlow, now a behavioural-health platform, so the judges have backed a health-tech company before.
opportunities.eligibility: US military veteran-owned. The business must be NO OLDER THAN THREE YEARS on the day of the competition, 7 December 2026 — an age ceiling, not a floor, which is why a company too young for most veteran grants qualifies here.
documents: Proof of veteran status (DD-214 or equivalent)
A 2-minute narrated pitch video — a pitch, not a promo
A deck of 10 slides or fewer: market, product/service, go-to-market, customers, financials, key risks
Evidence the business is under three years old as of 7 Dec 2026

opportunities.name: Intuit IDEAS — Virtual Military Veteran & Military-Spouse Cohort (2026-27)
opportunities.agency: Intuit (QuickBooks / Mailchimp / TurboTax / Credit Karma), with Zella Life coaching
opportunities.amount: $5,000 cash grant paid at completion of the 12-month program, plus a technology grant for hardware. Also free Intuit software, monthly coaching and workshops
opportunities.summary: C CORPORATIONS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE (Intuit's TurboTax community guide), so check Vybe's entity type first. If Vybe is an LLC or S corp, apply to the nationwide virtual military cohort as a veteran-owned business. The application is free and short, and Intuit says rolling. The $5,000 is paid at completion, not on selection. A 'technology grant for hardware' is part of the package, which helps a hardware company. Intuit's guide says businesses with at least one year of operation and active customers do best. That is preferred, not required, but it is a weak spot for a pre-revenue company under a year old.
opportunities.eligibility: Registered US small business. The city cohorts are limited to Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, DFW, LA, NYC, Philadelphia, San Diego and West Virginia. A separate virtual cohort takes veteran- and military-spouse-owned businesses nationwide, so it is open to Akron. Intuit's own community guide says C corporations and nonprofits are not eligible. The program runs 12 months, and the cash comes at the end.
documents: Online IDEAS application, selecting the virtual military cohort
Veteran/military-spouse status (not stated how it is verified)
QuickBooks onboarding if selected (per Intuit's guide)

opportunities.amount: $1,000 micro-grant + a free place on Passport Community ($1,499) or Zebra Leadership ($1,699). $20,000 fund, 20 finalists.

Evidence of 2-100 employees and under $5M revenue

opportunities.name: Blake Family Military & Veterans Pitch Competition (Clemson, 2nd annual)
opportunities.agency: Clemson University Brook T. Smith Launchpad (Blake family gift)
opportunities.summary: IN-PERSON FINAL AT CLEMSON, SC ON 6 NOV (the page does not say whether travel is covered). opportunities.name: Pave HER Way — Disruptor Award 2026 (inaugural)
opportunities.amount: Up to $90,000 per award, up to 5 awards; the amount is set at Pave HER Way's discretion. (The sister Financial Aid Award gives up to $30,000. You can apply to one, not both.)
opportunities.summary: THIS IS AN INDIVIDUAL / CHARITABLE-PURPOSE AWARD, NOT A GRANT TO THE COMPANY, AND IT IS ABOVE THE $25K BAND. The application deadline is only two weeks away.

The project must have 'clear public benefit for women and girls' in a charitable area; health, science and technology are listed. Interviews are virtual the week of 16–20 Nov and are mandatory. Winners join a 24-month mentorship of about 5 hours a month. Funds go to the individual or to an eligible sponsoring organization.
documents: Proof of citizenship or residency if a semifinalist (passport, birth certificate, naturalization certificate or green card)
Availability for a virtual interview 16–20 Nov

opportunities.name: Army xTech|Search 10
opportunities.agency: U.S. Army FUZE xTech Program, ASA(ALT)
opportunities.amount: Up to $1,000,000 in non-dilutive cash prizes across the competition: $5,000 to each of up to 50 semifinalists, a further $20,000 to each of up to 20 finalists, then $200,000 / $100,000 / $50,000 to first, second and third. Finalists may also submit a Phase I Army SBIR or STTR proposal worth up to $300,000.
opportunities.summary: BEST LIVE ITEM ON THE BOARD, and the deadline is 19 Oct at 5pm ET. It is an OPEN-TOPIC competition — you are not fitting a product to a stated problem — and one of the four named priority portfolios is 'Immersive and Wearables: smart electronic devices that can be worn by or attached to the user to gather data or provide insight', which is Vybe's category described by the Army in its own words. Four rounds: white paper by 19 Oct, virtual semifinal pitch 18-29 Jan 2027, finals at eMerge Americas in Miami 2-4 Mar 2027, then the SBIR/STTR window to 30 Apr. THE ONE GATE TO READ CAREFULLY: technologies falling EXCLUSIVELY within the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command portfolio — military operational medicine, clinical and rehabilitative medicine, infectious disease, CBRN — are excluded. Vybe's honest position is a commercial consumer wearable with a dual-use readiness application, not a medical technology, which is both true and the only framing that clears this exclusion. Do not describe it as a medical or diagnostic capability to sound more serious; that is the sentence that makes it ineligible. Judges compare unlike technologies, so the published evaluation emphasis is commercial traction, a defensible technical advantage, a direct line to an Army need, and a credible transition path.
opportunities.eligibility: For-profit US small business, more than 50% owned AND controlled by US citizens or permanent residents, 500 or fewer employees including affiliates. The submission must not be substantially the same as a proposal funded, being funded, or pending award at another federal agency. One submission per entity. No fee, and no equity is taken.
documents: Concept white paper via the xTech portal (Section IV of the RFI PDF states the format; the PDF was not readable from here)
Eligibility attestation: for-profit, >50% US-citizen owned and controlled, <=500 employees
Disclosure of any similar proposal funded or pending at another federal agency
SAM.gov UEI and a CAGE code for the follow-on SBIR/STTR stage

opportunities.name: DoW SBIR / STTR Specific Topics — Release 6 (26.BX / 26.BZ / 26.TX / 26.TZ)
opportunities.agency: Department of the Air Force — AFWERX / SpaceWERX, via the Defense SBIR/STTR Innovation Portal
opportunities.amount: Phase I feasibility study, then Phase II prototype; non-dilutive contract money, no equity taken
opportunities.summary: LIVE WINDOW, CLOSES 21 OCT. Eligibility is the same test Vybe already passed for xTech|Search 10, and the 26.BX solicitation family is literally the one xTech's follow-on topic sits in. THE WORK HERE IS NOT WRITING, IT IS READING: these are SPECIFIC topics, not an open topic, so the whole question is whether any Release 6 topic fits a consumer wearable and its interpretation layer without requiring a clinical or diagnostic posture. Open the Release 6 topic list on DSIP first and decide that before drafting anything. If nothing fits, the thing to wait for is an OPEN TOPIC cycle, which takes any dual-use technology — none is open as of today, and the published schedule shows only Specific Topics and Strategic Breakthrough, the latter needing a prior Phase II. Note Phase I is a three-month feasibility study with a structured curriculum and a kickoff meeting, and it does NOT require an existing DAF customer: finding one is part of the work. Letters of support from government personnel are not required but are read.
opportunities.eligibility: For-profit US small business, 500 or fewer employees including affiliates, more than 50% owned AND controlled by US citizens or permanent residents, building a DUAL-USE technology. The principal investigator's primary employment — more than 50% — must be with the small business. All R&D must be performed in the United States. One proposal per solicitation, and you cannot submit under both Air Force and Space Force topics in the same cycle. SAM.gov registration is required before award.
documents: Proposal on the mandatory AFWERX template — submissions that deviate from it are not evaluated
SAM.gov registration (required before award, not before submission)
Phase I work plan: scope, task outline, deliverables, kickoff within 30 days, preliminary and final report
Disclosure of any essentially equivalent work funded or pending elsewhere

opportunities.name: Ohio TechCred
opportunities.amount: up to $1,000 per employee credential, capped at $30,000 per application period
opportunities.summary: CORRECTED 30 SEP: this row previously read "Ohio-based employers only", which understates it badly. The real test is a non-residential Ohio premises plus Ohio-resident W-2 employees on the state payroll system — a three-person startup working from home, or one whose founders draw no W-2 wage, fails on both counts before the credentials are even chosen. Confirm those two facts before anything else. The window is 9:00am 1 Oct to 3:00pm 30 Oct 2026. Reimburses technology credentials for current OR prospective employees rather than funding the business, so it is a cost offset on upskilling, and the employer pays the training provider first and claims afterwards. The programme was reframed in July 2026 with a tighter technology-focused credential definition, updated employer eligibility and a new eligible-provider list, so any advice written before then is stale. The application does not ask you to name individuals — only headcounts per credential and average wages before and after. It is competitive and merit-based, not first come, first served, and reviews can take up to 90 days. Drafted as the `techcred` packet.
opportunities.eligibility: FOUR GATES, NOT ONE. The employer must be registered with the Ohio Secretary of State; must have a PHYSICAL, NON-RESIDENTIAL business location in Ohio; must employ Ohio-resident W-2 employees reported to the Ohio Unemployment Insurance Office; and must withhold Ohio income tax for them. Independent contractors and 1099 workers do not count, and an employer exempt from those reporting requirements is not eligible at all. One application per federal tax ID per period. Training must come from a provider on Ohio's eligible list, and that provider must be independent of the employer.
documents: Federal tax ID, Ohio Payee ID from ohiopays.ohio.gov, and Ohio Secretary of State charter or entity number
Physical non-residential Ohio business address and number of Ohio W-2 employees
Chosen credential from the eligible list, or a full case for a new one, with the training provider's own documentation
Per-credential training and certification costs, and the reimbursement amount requested (max $1,000 each)
Headcounts of incumbent and prospective employees per credential, with average wages before and after

3–5 minute video demo or pitch deck

Three finalists pitch in person on Nov 12, 2026 in Orlando at their own cost. Judges score reimbursement potential and fit with clinical workflow, so this one leans clinical.
opportunities.eligibility: Open to startups, early-stage companies, researchers, clinicians and entrepreneurs 'regardless of professional background or geographic location' whose solution connects to physical medicine and rehabilitation. The solution must be past the idea stage (working prototype, pilot data, early traction or other progress). Application fee: not stated. Travel is not covered.
documents: Submittable profile, then the online application
Evidence of stage of development (prototype, pilot data or traction)
